blog_summary: Adrian Colyer reviews a survey paper on Dynamic and Stochastic Vehicle Routing Problems (DSVRP), highlighting its relevance to modern logistics and delivery businesses. The paper distinguishes between static VRP (where all parameters are known upfront) and dynamic/stochastic variants, where real-time data (e.g., traffic, customer requests) and predictive models improve routing efficiency. Key insights include the significant performance gains from incorporating dynamic elements (up to 60% improvement) and the importance of predictive models for customer demand. The survey categorizes DSVRP approaches into preprocessed and online decision-making, with event-driven re-optimization often outperforming time-driven methods. The blog also notes gaps in research, particularly the understudied combination of multiple stochastic factors (e.g., traffic and demand). Colyer speculates on the potential of reinforcement learning for end-to-end decision-making.
paper_title: A survey on dynamic and stochastic vehicle routing problems
